sources.title: Star Citizen Single-Player Spinoff Squadron 42 Reemerges With Flashy New Trailer, Steam Wishlists, and Cast Confirmation
sources.text: Star Citizen developer Cloud Imperium Games has pulled back the curtain on single-player spinoff Squadron 42 with a new cinematic trailer, the launch of Steam wishlists, and a full cast reveal. Squadron 42 is the story-driven off-shoot of space sim Star Citizen, which Cloud Imperium Games has worked on for the last 12 years. Its 12-year development is led by Chris Roberts, creator of the Wing Commander series. Indeed, Squadron 42 is a spiritual successor to Wing Commander, and like the Wing Commander games, Squadron 42 features a string of Hollywood stars, such as Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Gillian Anderson, Ben Mendelsohn, and Henry Cavill. The game fuses space combat, first-person shooter action, and a character-driven narrative supported by full performance capture. CIG said the performances are woven directly into gameplay, so you won’t just see those famous actors within cinematics. And here’s what to expect from the structure of the game: The trailer shows a decent amount of gameplay, including first-person sections, some of which involve platforming and puzzle solving, ship customization, off duty activities, a hacking mini-game, and a glimpse at narrative choices. Ian Duncan, best known for playing Todd Todmore on BBC comedy Broken News, is the male player character, and prolific video game actor Alix Wilton Regan (Samantha Traynor in Mass Effect 3, the female Inquisitor in Dragon Age: Inquisition, Aya in Assassin's Creed Origins, and Lara Croft in the upcoming Tomb Raider games) plays the female player character. In August, CIG delayed Squadron 42 to Q2 2027 , with Roberts insisting it wouldn’t get the attention it deserves if it came out at the end of 2026 because of November’s GTA 6. "At CitizenCon 2024, we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," Roberts said at the time. "But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had 12 years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6. While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage." The delay announcement came hot on the heels of a disastrous Star Citizen developer livestream that went radically off the rails . After early access players complained of bugs and issues with a new update to the game, CIG held a stream to show the "intended" version of the experience, only to be met with the same issues, if not worse. It led to passive-aggressive comments between the developers themselves and an uncomfortable tension in the air. Star Citizen crossed the $1 billion raised barrier in May — a significant milestone that came shortly after a $5,000 virtual spaceship you couldn’t actually fly in-game went on sale. It’s since raised a further $50 million. Star Citizen is considered one of the most controversial projects in all video games. Over the 14 years since its crowdfunding drive began, Star Citizen has been called many things, including a scam by those who wonder whether it will ever properly launch. Its virtual ships, some of which cost thousands of dollars, are often the focus of criticism. But its loyal fanbase insist it's one of the most compelling space sims around, and continue to pump millions of dollars into the project via ship sales. Star Citizen itself remains without a release window. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Squadron 42 has a Steam page
sources.text: Star Citizen's singleplayer mode gets a new trailer and more signs of life. In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6 . There was a certain amount of skepticism about the reason for the delay, thanks in part to a recent Star Citizen livestream being declared a disaster , but also because, well. These games have had so many release dates the changes have their own wiki page . There's something concrete about having Squadron 42 getting a Steam page though, with system requirements and everything. Those system requirements are charmingly old-fashioned, with no mention of ray tracing-capable GPUs or DirectX 12. Although the install size of 150GB is still pretty hefty. ( Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is apparently going to be 200GB , oof.) There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42. So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight in Game of Thrones, and other people who probably filmed most of their scenes a solid decade ago now. We also get to see a fair bit of the male version of the player-character, who will doubtless BroShep his way into most of the promos even though I'll be picking the one voiced by Alix Wilton Regan instead. The Steam page lists Squadron 42's release date as Q2 2027, and I'd love to see it actually release on that date and be the solid combo of Wing Commander and Half-Life 2 that happens to have Gillian Anderson and Henry Cavill in the cutscenes that's being promised here. It could happen. stories.title: Developer Goes Into Debt Spending $1,000 A Day To Keep Steam Demo For AI-Fueled Driving Sim Going
stories.summary: Hoping to launch next year, Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is prematurely sending its creators into the red over exhaustive token use

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Developer Goes Into Debt Spending $1,000 A Day To Keep Steam Demo For AI-Fueled Driving Sim Going
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is an upcoming DMV simulator where players, riding passenger, instruct a chaotic young student to pass their exam. Developers Easy Fox are embracing AI for the project, the titular sister a live chat bot that the player is instructing. Beyond contention for the tech, Easy Fox are finding that the mere demo for the game is proving to be problematic, as accounting for the token usage is forcing them into debt . “Over the past month, the number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold,” reads the Steam pageâs latest update . “Thank you so much for giving our game far more attention than we ever expected. This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably.” As the update explains, the game originally patched players through to a chat bot operating on Googleâs Gemini. With no cost barrier between them and the curious, players of the demo were triggering limit-use errors, Google informing Easy Fox that thereâs no easy way out. Switching to the competing OpenAI model, while hoping to finding a fix with Gemini, is proving to be the least of their problems. Easy Fox says the surge of players has forced them to take out a bank loan to keep the demo operating. Maintaining the demo is apparently costing them more than $1,000 a day, which they admit they will have to factor into pricing the final product. While a number of game developers have flocked to AI to create in-game assets and code on the back-end, Teach My Little Sister is a more unique case. Leveraging an agent for sustained real-time gameplay, the game has found an expensive way to recreate what Lifeline and Hey You, Pikachu! accomplished over 20 years ago. “We want to continue operating the demo and would love for more people to enjoy it,” writes Easy Fox. “However, we are a small team of four, and financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release. We have not made that decision at this time.” The update also addresses complaints that, even in a game based around calamity, the AI fueled sister is not following instructions as desired. While a microcosm of it, the financial strain is an amusing illustration of one of AIâs biggest white elephant. That is, no oneâs sure how to make money off of it. While proliferating in short video content, horrifying fast food posters and visual assets devs “meant to take out,” the firms themselves are running purely on investments, not generating profit. The amount of resources needed to keep these computers burning continually outweighs what the public is otherwise willing to spend to see SpongeBob murder Shrek . Over the last year, AI firms have been forced to adjust, adding new premiums to their service, the so-called “tokenpocalypse.” With the global economy now held hostage by the industry, the burdens of the tech continue to put people on edge. Easy Fox are being taught a swift lesson on something the global population is likely going to learn the hard way. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per month just to keep its demo running
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot. One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry in facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly. At least, that's the theory. Developer Easy Fox released a demo for Teach My Little Sister How To Drive back in February, but in the past month the game has seen a surge in players, which has had an interesting knock-on effect for the demo. "The number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold," Easy Fox explained in a Steam post , adding. "This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably." Easy Fox goes on to explain that it is "spending over $1,000 per day on AI services for the demo", as players burn through tokens prompting the LLM by proxy. Easy Fox claims that figure "isn't because each player is particularly expensive to support", but rather that "so many people are playing." As a result of this, Easy Fox has "taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running". Yet even this may not be sufficient to support the demo long term. "Financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release," Easy Fox says, though the studio stresses it has "not made that decision at this time". According to FRVR, that twentyfold increase in players amounts to 450 concurrent. While the overall player numbers will be higher than that, it isn't an enormous figure, and it makes me wonder how financially viable the game will be when it is released. Easy Fox says it will "account for expected AI usage in the game's price". But it also says that players "will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game". That might work in the short term, but surely those token costs are going to pile up over time. It's also worth noting that AI token costs are highly unpredictable , with even large companies like Microsoft and Uber struggling to accurately predict the cost and burn rate of their own internal token use. In its Steam post, Easy Fox says it's looking into options like introducing local AI models for players with "sufficiently capable GPUs". But that's only going to be a fraction of the player-base. Personally, I think the fact that it revolves specifically around chatting with another character makes this a more sensible application than in Where Winds Meet, where the chatbots don't factor into the game design in any meaningful way. It's much more reminiscent of early chatbot-based social sim Façade . But the very fact it reminds me of Façade makes me wonder whether the game needs a premium LLM connected to it to achieve its goal. Easy Fox states that current design problems being addressed include "dialogue that feels too artificial and breaks immersion" and "commands being carried out incorrectly, such as turning right when asked to turn left." All of which seems like it could be solved with a good voice actor and a sufficiently rich dialogue system. stories.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
stories.summary: O final de Townfall é determinado por algumas ações ao longo do jogo

sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
sources.text: Silent Hill: Townfall , o novo spin-off desenvolvido pela Screen Burnem parceria com a Konami, chega para expandir o universo da franquia em um cenário inédito . Desta vez, estamos na isolada ilha escocesa de St. Amelia, em 1996. O protagonista, Simon Ordell, é convocado de volta à cidade para “colocar as coisas em ordem”, mas encontra apenas uma névoa densa cobrindo ruas aparentemente abandonadas. Apesar de não se passar na cidade famosa da franquia, o tipo de contexto é basicamente o mesmo. Seguindo a tradição de jogos da série, Townfall não conta com um final único. Em vez disso, as ações do jogador ao longo da campanha determinam qual desfecho a história vai tomar. Para te ajudar a entender melhor o conceito, listamos os todos os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall e te contamos o que é necessário para conseguir cada um deles. Confira! Como revelado previamente pelos desenvolvedores, o jogo conta com 5 finais diferentes, sendo que 2 são secretos. Assim como em jogos anteriores da série, as decisões tomadas pelo jogador ao longo da aventura é que definem o desfecho, até para que o final pareça coerente com a experiência vivida durante a partida. Não existe uma escolha explícita em algum momento marcante do enredo que define isso, já que o final é determinado por alguns elementos diferentes. O sistema acompanha o comportamento do jogador durante toda a partida, incluindo o quanto ele explora e investiga St. Amelia e o quão agressivo ele é ao ser confrontado por inimigos, em contraste com evitar ou fugir dos combates. Essa abordagem lembra diretamente o clássico Silent Hill 2 , em que o final também refletia padrões de comportamento e não escolhas de diálogo, por exemplo. Dos 5 desfechos possíveis , 3 estão disponíveis já na primeira vez que você zera a campanha , sem necessidade de repetir o jogo. Já os outros 2 finais secretos exigem uma segunda campanha jogada no modo New Game Plus. Esses 3 finais “normais” são chamados de Justice, Forever e Abandoned e são considerados os desfechos principais da trama de Simon. Eles são determinados exclusivamente pela relação entre quantos inimigos o jogador elimina durante a partida e quantas descobertas, como pistas e documentos, ele coleta ao longo do caminho. O tempo de jogo ou uso de itens de cura não influencia nesse resultado. Também é bom mencionar que que esse equilíbrio entre mortes e descobertas afeta apenas a cena final antes dos créditos, sem alterar outras cenas ou a progressão da história ao longo da campanha. Até por isso, você é que tem lembrar de como quer abordar o jogo para conseguir o final desejado. Conforme mencionamos, além dos 3 finais principais, o jogo reserva 2 desfechos extras classificados como secretos , chamados de Dog e Sci-fi. Quem é fã veterano da franquia Silent Hill sabe que esses são finais absolutamente clássicos e colocados no jogo apenas como uma brincadeira extra para o jogador se divertir. Por serem uma piada, é necessário zerar o game uma vez para conseguir um final sério e, então, zerá-lo uma segunda vez no New Game Plus para ter acesso aos desfechos secretos. Como explicado acima, o sistema de finais de Townfall não depende de escolhas de diálogo ou momentos de decisão específicos, mas sim do comportamentos do jogador ao longo de toda a campanha. Para facilitar, nós listamos o que é necessário para cada um. O final Justice é considerado por muitos como o desfecho “bom” da história. Ele é obtido ao final de uma campanha em que o número de descobertas, na forma de pistas e documentos coletados, é significativamente maior do que o número de inimigos eliminados. A boa notícia é que é possível ter dezenas de eliminações e ainda assim alcançar esse final, até porque alguns confrontos ao longo da aventura são praticamente inevitáveis. Por isso, só tente ter certeza de que a quantidade de descobertas seja bem superior. O final Forever é tratado como o desfecho “normal” do jogo. Ele surge quando a quantidade de descobertas é apenas ligeiramente maior do que a quantidade de eliminações ao término da campanha. Diferente do Justice, aqui a margem entre pistas coletadas e inimigos mortos é bem mais estreita, exigindo um equilíbrio mais cuidadoso por parte do jogador ao longo da aventura. Já o Abandoned é considerado o final “ruim” da história. Ele ocorre sempre que o número de inimigos eliminados supera o número de descobertas feitas até o fim do jogo. Para quem opta por um estilo de jogo mais agressivo, ignorando documentos e pistas em favor do combate direto, esse desfecho é praticamente garantido. O final “Dog” é um dos desfechos secretos, exclusivos do New Game Plus. Ele é desbloqueado ao encontrar três moedas especiais espalhadas por diferentes áreas da cidade durante a nova campanha. Com as moedas em mãos, você precisa depositá-las em cofres em formato de cachorro, ligados a uma instituição de cães-guia presente no cenário do jogo. Completar essa sequência de itens substitui o final principal que o jogador obteria normalmente. O Sci-fi é o segundo final secreto, também restrito ao New Game Plus. Para obtê-lo, é necessário interagir com três livros específicos escondidos em diferentes pontos da campanha, resolver um quebra-cabeça de porta usando um código, e por fim utilizar um item especial obtido nesse processo em um painel eletrônico próximo ao fim da aventura. Diferente dos demais finais, o Sci-fi é acionado antes da batalha final, pulando completamente esse confronto e levando direto ao desfecho. Se não quiser spoilers sobre os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall, é melhor pular essa parte do nosso guia! No final “Justice”, Simon consegue encarar os traumas do seu passado de frente, encontrando uma resolução pacífica e libertadora para a sua culpa. No final “Forever”, o protagonista se recusa a aceitar os fatos totalmente e decide permanecer preso na névoa e nas memórias da ilha. No final Abandoned, dominado pela raiva e violência, Simon sucumbe totalmente ao pesadelo e se torna parte do ciclo de sofrimento do loc

sources.title: It looks like Wing Commander 3 is getting a remaster, after EA producer discovers the original FMV source tapes in the company's archives
sources.text: Plans for a 30th Anniversary Edition of the classic space sim were revealed at Portland Gaming Expo. Typical, isn't it? You wait ages for new information on a Chris Roberts-directed space combat sim, and then two lots come along at once. Less than 24 hours after Cloud Imperium Games surprise-released a glossy trailer for Star Citizen 's single-player spinoff Squadron 42, it now appears that Roberts' 1994 classic Wing Commander 3 is getting a remaster courtesy of EA. The project is headed up by EA producer Jim Vessella, who revealed the remaster during a presentation at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo . The remaster will include cutscenes based on Wing Commander 3's original FMV recordings, after Vessella discovered 600 source tapes while digitising EA's video archive. In a post on Bluesky, Steve Lin, a board member of the Video Game History Foundation , shared an image of Vessella's talk , which shows a projector slide detailing the remaster's features. The remaster is called Wing Commander 3: Heart of the Tiger—30 th anniversary edition. A slightly unfortunate name, given Wing Commander 3's was released 32 years ago. As for those features, the slide says the remaster will include both source and upscaled versions of the game's FMVs, and will include "Kilrathi Saga integration"—which presumably means it will bundle in Wing Commanders 1 & 2 and their various expansion packs. The remaster will also run at 60 FPS and—in additional details shared by Lin —will feature controller support and will be released on Steam, GOG, and the EA app. Re-release of Wing Commander III coming out with video taken from the original tapes courtesy of a restoration project led by Jim Vessella who has been digitizing the EA video archive Alongside Wing Commander 4, Wing Commander 3 is generally regarded as the strongest entry in the series, heightening the cinematic flair of the games with a stellar voice cast including Mark Hamill and John Rhys-Davies (both of whom also appear in Squadron 42). It's notable for being one of the few games from the era to actually tell a good story using FMVs , so the fact that Vessella has managed to retrieve to the original videos is especially exciting. It's an interesting project to emerge from EA, given the publisher hasn't shown a huge interest in reviving or revisiting its older games. Despite being fantastic, EA's Dead Space remake didn't sell well enough for the publisher to greenlight the same treatment for the sequel, and in recent years the company has consolidated resources around heavy hitters like Battlefield and EA Sports FC. So is this simply a passion project by Vessella that he managed to get greenlit? Or the start of something bigger? Either way, I'm glad to see it happening. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. sources.text: GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back with another video, this time with a naked Lucia taking a parachute jump off a rooftop. The five-minute clip was posted on ResetEra a few days after CyberLeek's 25-minute video of Jason , and a day after the leaker threatened to release a full playable build . Note: there are some mild spoilers pertaining to what you might do in GTA 6 below. The video - which I'm afraid I'm not going to post here - reportedly opens with CyberLeek driving through Vice City in a black-and-white car, before Lucia gets out in nowt but her birthday suit. As with Jason, nobody reacts to her, and as we noted last time, whoever is playing seems to have access to a dev menu, which means a naked Lucia could be a debug feature rather than something you'll be able to do in the open world. Lucia then heads up some stairs to an ATM, where she beats up a passer-by and takes their money. The machine shows a $15,000 limit and a Buckme logo (thanks, TheGamer ). She goes into a nearby building, where a construction worker asks if she's with the guy on the roof, and takes the elevator after a short exchange. Following a phone call, she makes her way to the roof and is handed a parachute before jumping off. CyberLeek isn't a natural at that part of the game. The first jump drifts well off course and ends in a crash into a building, while the second gets closer to the target but sails past the landing point. The video also includes an in-game ad for Buckme. CyberLeek has said they'll release the full build if their cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million . Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company, has been hunting for the person behind the leaks, and has tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity. GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on 19th November.

sources.text: New preview for one of the best films of the year stomps onto screens The ground is shaking, and people are running in every direction, which can only mean the big, angry fella known as the King of Monsters has returned, as revealed in a brand-new trailer for the eagerly anticipated Godzilla Minus Zero. Director Takashi Yamazaki returns to the camera with an all-new chapter that picks up after Godzilla Minus One, as post-war Japan struggles to get back on its feet after Godzilla's initial attack, only to face a new foe: King Ghidorah. Naturally, Godzilla regenerates, proving this town isn't big enough for these two building-bashing monsters and that only a battle for supremacy can settle things. GamesRadar+ has already passed a verdict, and we think it's easily one of the best films of the year, and we're not the only ones. With a nearly perfect Rotten Tomatoes score , it's clear Yamazaki is delivering on his previous effort, and the cast is too. Returning to take on the giant beasties are Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Yuki Yamada, Kuranosuke Sasaki, Sakura Ando, and Miou Tanaka. Joining them in the chaos this time around are also Min Tanaka, Masami Nagasawa, and Jun Kunimura. The film also marks a first in Godzilla's history: the only R-rated Godzilla flick to date , ensuring severe casualties as the giant fire-breathing lizard takes on the triple threat of King Ghidorah. Speaking to the decision, Yamazaki assured that "There were certain scenes that, for me as a director, were so essential to the film. Censoring it or cutting it was just not an option for me." It was the right call, but we'll see how he handles things when Godzilla: Minus Zero arrives in theaters on November 6. To prep for what's in store, check out our full review. sources.text: A new threat emerges in the latest trailer for Godzilla Minus Zero Less than a day after the movie's New York Comic Con panel, a second Godzilla Minus Zero trailer was released. Like the previous trailer, it suggests that Godzilla isn't the only monster threat that humans will have to contend with in this highly anticipated sequel. The trailer begins with a doctor suggesting that Noriko had "no business surviving" the events of Godzilla Minus One before cutting to Koichi flying through a supernatural storm, lifting entire houses far up into the air. Cue a sizzle reel of people running from or discussing how they're scared of the impending threat, all culminating with a massive atomic breath attack from Godzilla. That said, Godzilla doesn't seem to be the only monster humans will face in this movie. The trailer's description alludes to "a new threat," and while it doesn't show another creature, it hints at one. Namely, while Godzilla's attacks have a blue hue in Godzilla Minus One and this trailer, we also see beams attacking civilians and destroying a bomb at certain points in the trailer that look more yellow or lightning-like. If you want to avoid spoilers for Godzilla Minus Zero before watching it in theaters, stop reading here! As Polygon's review and comments from the filmmakers at New York Comic Con confirm, Gidorah plays a major role in Godzilla Minus Zero. Ever since the three-headed monster debuted in 1964, it has been one of the Godzilla franchise's most recognizable characters and has faced off against Godzilla in many different movies. We last saw Gidorah in 2019's American-made Godzilla: King of the Monsters , so it'll be exciting to see how a Japanese filmmaker like Takashi Yamazaki reinterprets the character for his series' post-World War 2 setting. I absolutely adored the first movie, so that's more than enough of an enticing prospect to get me to see this movie in IMAX. Godzilla Minus Zero will come to theaters on Nov. 6.

You can always find this collection hub in the XBOX Store and on XBOX.com/IndieSelects. Halloween has never been just about scares. Sure, there’s plenty of room for heart-pounding frights, but it’s also a season that celebrates imagination, creativity, and stepping into worlds beyond the ordinary. This month, indie developers embraced that spirit in unforgettable ways. For October, the ID@XBOX team has curated six standout Indie Selects that invite you to discover mysterious realms, conquer new challenges, and uncover stories waiting to be told. From epic battles and eldritch horrors to cozy puzzles and island adventures, each game offers a richly crafted world filled with surprises around every corner. So, whether you’re seeking thrills, mystery, or a new adventure to get lost in, here are this month’s Indie Selects (in no particular order): Mortal Shell II is still unapologetically challenging, but combat feels faster and more aggressive this time around. The removal of the traditional stamina gauge means encounters aren’t simply about waiting for a bar to refill. You can stay in the fight, combining melee weapons, sidearms, abilities and brutal executions. It makes combat feel considerably more fluid than before. The world has grown too. Rather than simply pushing you down a predetermined path, Mortal Shell II encourages exploration across a compact, interconnected open world filled with hidden areas, dungeons, weapons, upgrades and, naturally, plenty of horrible things waiting to ruin your afternoon. What I particularly enjoy is that exploration feels connected to progression. Finding another Shell isn’t just another collectible checked off a list. It can completely change how you approach the game. Weapons offer extensive upgrade paths as well, giving you plenty of room to shape your own approach to combat. Mortal Shell II certainly isn’t interested in making life easy for you, but there’s something satisfying about gradually turning the tables. You go from cautiously approaching every new enemy to becoming the nightmare wandering through their world. If you enjoy dark fantasy, exploration, challenging combat and the satisfaction of mastering a game that initially seems determined to destroy you, Mortal Shell II is absolutely worth having on your radar. If you’ve ever wondered what it would be like to assemble your dream team of benders and settle legendary rivalries yourself , Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is ready to make that happen. This 2D tag-team fighter brings together iconic characters from “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Legend of Korra,” combining elemental bending, flashy special moves, and fast-paced team combat into an experience that’s easy to jump into and rewarding to master. As a longtime fan of the Avatar universe, this game immediately grabbed my attention. There’s something incredibly satisfying about watching beloved characters leap from the screen into a fighting game that feels so true to the world they come from. From the first match, I found myself grinning at familiar abilities, character interactions, and bending styles brought to life in exciting new ways. What impressed me most is how distinct every fighter feels. Experimenting with different team combinations kept me coming back for “just one more match” as I discovered new strategies and synergies. Fans of games like Dragon Ball FighterZ , Marvel vs. Capcom , and Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid will recognize the thrill of building a team and learning how each character complements the others. There’s plenty to learn with its tag mechanics and assists, but the journey of improving feels rewarding and keeps every victory exciting. Whether you grew up with “Avatar: The Last Airbender,” fell in love with “The Legend of Korra,” or simply enjoy energetic team-based fighting games, Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game captures the heart of the franchise while delivering a fun and action-packed experience that’s hard to put down. From the moment I started playing Mewgenics , I knew I was in for a wild ride. From Edmund McMillen, the developer behind The Binding of Isaac , Super Meat Boy , and The End is Nigh , Mewgenics is a roguelike tactical turn-based RPG presented in a unique and cartoonish macabre art style, filled with dark humor and clever references. Mewgenics offers a staggering amount of content that easily demands over a hundred hours of playtime, complete with deep strategy and a generational breeding system (yes, you breed mutant cats). The game hooks you right away with its chaotic setup, you’re managing a house full of mutated cats and sending them out on tactical, grid-based runs. Every item, skill, and attribute is randomized, meaning no two runs ever play out the same way. When your cats survive a brutal dungeon crawl, they bring back scars and mutations that you can pass down to future generations. Breeding the ultimate mutant cat squad and trying to balance their weird genetic traits became an obsession. The dark and sometimes graphic humor and the relentless difficulty might not be for everyone, but for me, it hit the right buttons. sources.text: The hit RPG Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection , currently available on XBOX Series X|S, will launch on XBOX on PC on November 18 , 2026, with Xbox Play Anywhere support. This will allow players to enjoy the game on XBOX Series X|S, Windows 11 PCs, and compatible handheld gaming devices at no additional cost. Players can pick up right where they left off on their preferred device, with all save data, additional game content, achievements, and more carried over seamlessly. Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection is a turn-based RPG set in the world of Monster Hunter, allowing players to enjoy an adventure on a larger scale than ever before. The story follows the prince or princess of Azuria, the only Rathalos Rider in the country, and Eleanor, the princess of Vermeil, each setting out for the forbidden ground with their own hopes and convictions, embark on a journey to uncover the truth of the world. After making an historic discovery, the protagonist, a trained Rider, sets out on a journey to learn more about the various situations unfolding across the world. Players can enjoy a variety of features, including evolving turn-based battles and Habitat Restoration, which allows players to release monsters back into the wild and change their Ecosystem rank. Even after taking your time to enjoy the main story, there is still more to experience. After updating the game to the latest version and loading your cleared save data, you can take on a high-difficulty version of the final boss battle. If you can beat this challenge, Royal versions of nearly all monsters will appear throughout the various areas of the map. In addition, Royal Invasive Monsters and Royal Calamitous Elder Dragons will also appear, offering highly challenging battles. Take on these formidable foes with your well-trained roster of monsters. The DLC Side Story: Rudy is also available now. This content is included in the Deluxe Edition, Premium Deluxe Edition, and Deluxe Kit, so if you own any of these, you can download and enjoy this DLC at no additional cost. Experience the story behind the origins of Rudy, who travels alongside the protagonist as Royal Palico. Thanks to the support of our loyal fans, Monster Hunter Stories celebrates its 10th anniversary on October 8th. We would like to sincerely thank everyone who has supported the series over the years. To mark this special occasion, we are delighted to share a special commemorative visual with you. We look forward to your continued support of the Monster Hunter Stories series. Three titles have been released to date in this RPG series where players become a Rider, forge bonds with monsters, raise them, and live alongside them while exploring the world of Monster Hunter. Each title weaves an epic story centered around the bonds between humans and monsters. A story of beginnings, following the protagonist as they set out into the outside world alongside Rathalos, they have bonded with, growing into a Rider along the way. Raised in a village of Riders who raise monsters and live alongside them, the protagonist overcomes a series of trials, grows into a Rider, and eventually sets out into the outside world. There, they encounter a world of Hunters who hunt monsters to make a living. Though initially bewildered by this way of life, the protagonist begins living alongside the Hunters, sharing in their daily lives and forging a connection between Hunters and Riders. An ominous shadow known as the Black Blight, a calamity that drives monsters into a frenzy, begins to creep across the world. The everyday lives and environment that were once taken for granted undergo serious changes, which gradually spread on a global scale. Riders and Hunters are put to the test as they face the responsibilities entrusted to them. The key lies in the Kinship Stone possessed by Riders and its hidden power. As the story unfolds, they draw closer to the truth of Redan’s Legacy, which contains the long-hidden origins of the Riders. A new Rider’s story of forging bonds with monsters. What awaits them: destruction or hope? In a world where all Rathalos have mysteriously flown away, the protagonist, a descendant of the great Rider Redan, has a fateful encounter with a young Wyverian girl, Ena, who entrusts them with an Egg. When the Rathalos finally hatches, its wings are black, just as the legend foretold, and its appearance is unmistakably that of Razewing Ratha. To uncover the truth behind the mysterious events unfolding across the world and the legend itself, the protagonists embark on a journey to weave a story of destruction and hope. Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection Azuria and Vermeil: two countries, on a path to destruction. When all hope seems lost, an egg is found. Inside is a Rathalos, a species thought to be extinct. But this quavering light of hope is quickly extinguished, giving way to the darkness of despair. Born from the egg is not a single Rathalos, but twins, bearing the Skyscale marking that hearkens back to the disastrous civil wat of 200 years prior. The natural world teeters on the verge of destruction with countless monster species facing extinction. In the shadow of these dark times, the flames of war rekindle. A Rider and their trusted Rathalos, buffeted by the winds of fate, set out on a journey for the truth. sources.text: This message was just sent to Team XBOX employees globally. At Town Hall on Tuesday, I talked about the four Cs and the choices we are making to put them into practice. You’ve seen a lot of our work on Core and Content. Today I want to share two leadership appointments supporting Creator and Connection. Kayleen Walters will transition from her role at Mojang to President of XP, a new XBOX division focused on how people experience our franchises beyond the games themselves, and Maria Angelidou-Smith will join XBOX as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft. Both will report to me. Kayleen has spent her career building entertainment franchises. Before XBOX, she spent 13 years at Lucasfilm helping guide Star Wars across films, products, and partnerships. At Minecraft, she helped grow consumer products into a multibillion-dollar business with more than 250 licensees and was Executive Producer of A Minecraft Movie , the biggest film in the U.S. last year and a top-five release worldwide. She is also a producer of the sequel. XP is a play on “Experience Points” and formalizes four investment areas for us: XBOX PICTURES for film and television adaptations; XBOX PRODUCTS for licensing and merchandise; XBOX PARTNERSHIPS for sponsors and brand partners; and XBOX PLACES for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences. Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place. Kayleen’s move also gave us time to think carefully about what Mojang needs in its next leader. Minecraft is one of the largest communities in entertainment. Hundreds of millions of people play, build, create, teach, watch, mod, run servers, and build businesses around Minecraft. The community doesn’t just consume the product. It helps shape what the product becomes. That was central to our search. Mojang already has an exceptional game development team that knows Minecraft and its players deeply. We wanted someone who has built products for communities at enormous scale, who is deeply technical, and who understands how creators, product, technology, and monetization come together. Maria brings a rare combination of those experiences. She spent nearly a decade at Meta, where she led Facebook Groups used by more than 1.8 billion people each month, as well as Events, Creators, Search, Profile, and Monetization. She later led product and technology at Personio and served as Chief Product Officer at Reddit, another of the world’s largest community platforms. She has built products used by billions of people and led product and engineering organizations through significant growth and change. Maria brings deep experience to Mojang, along with a respect for what makes Minecraft special. Her first priority will be learning from the teams and communities who know Minecraft best. She starts Monday, October 19. Please join me in congratulating Kayleen and welcoming Maria to XBOX!
